title: STAR: Sub-Entry Sharing-Aware TLB for Multi-Instance GPU
problem: NVIDIA's Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology shares the last-level TLB (L3 TLB) across all instances, causing performance degradation for co-running applications and inefficient sub-entry utilization before eviction.
motivation: Optimizing TLB resource sharing is critical for improving multi-tenant GPU performance and reducing address translation interference.
method: STAR dynamically manages TLB entry sharing by evaluating sub-entry utilization and adaptively switching between shared and non-shared states. It allows the 16 sub-entries within each L3 TLB entry to be flexibly shared across multiple base addresses, with the system adjusting allocation based on current workload demand patterns.
key_novelty: Dynamic sharing of TLB entries across multiple base addresses based on sub-entry utilization metrics, enabling adaptive optimization between shared and non-shared states.
contributions: Comprehensive analysis of L3 TLB sharing interference in NVIDIA MIG systems and its impact on multi-tenant performance
STAR mechanism for dynamic TLB sub-entry sharing and utilization optimization
Adaptive state transitions between shared and non-shared modes based on utilization patterns
28.7% average performance improvement across multi-tenant GPU workloads
limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Dynamic TLB entry sharing for multi-instance GPU optimization
